key_insight: Detonation-sprayed titanium dioxide based coatings can be tuned for roughness, thickness, and hydrophobicity by adjusting process parameters, with optimal settings yielding maximum water repellency.
engineering_relevance: The study provides practical process-parameter guidance for designing functional anti-wetting coating surfaces in thermal spray manufacturing.
method: Varied detonation spraying conditions, especially nozzle passage speed and spray distance.
Measured coating surface roughness, thickness, and contact angle to quantify hydrophobicity.
Fit empirical relationships, including inverse-power and parabolic dependencies, to predict surface characteristics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experimentally derived equations linking process parameters to roughness, thickness, and contact angle, enabling prediction of coating performance.
watch_item: The reported optimums are process- and material-specific, so transfer to other spray systems, substrates, or coating chemistries will require validation.
paper_title: Surface Characteristics of Titanium Based Coatings Obtained by Detonation Spraying Under Various Process Conditions
